title: The explorer who walked home alone across Antarctica
hook: A man fell into an Antarctic crevasse alone and hung by a rope
summary: In 1913 Douglas Mawson lost both companions in Antarctica, survived a crevasse fall alone, and reached base hours after his ship left.
sources: Wikipedia: Douglas Mawson; Australasian Antarctic Expedition. Ninnis fell into a crevasse in December 1912 with a sledge and most food; Mertz died in January 1913.
Australian Antarctic Division: Mawson fell into a crevasse, was held by his sledge rope, climbed out, reached Cape Denison in February 1913 after the Aurora had sailed; he stayed another winter.

lines.text: A man fell into an Antarctic crevasse, alone, and hung by a rope.
lines.caps: A man *fell | into a *crevasse, | alone, hanging *by a rope

lines.text: Douglas Mawson was a month from base, and both companions were dead.
One fell into a crevasse with the food. The other died on the trek.
Then the snow gave way under Mawson, and he dangled over darkness.
Somehow he climbed out, and kept walking.
He reached the base hours after his ship sailed away.
Six men had stayed behind, so he waited one more winter.

post.caption:
Mawson walked for weeks with no one beside him, then missed his ship by hours.
Would you have kept walking?
Follow @unt.oldfiles for a new untold story every day.
